Two Days in Dallas - Review
items.text:
## **Two Days in Dallas**

⚡️⚡️⚡️⚡️⚡️ 5/5 Zaps. Worth the visit if you can make the trek, one of my new favorite Bitcoin citys to visit, will be back again!

***

I’ll start with the places I went, move to the good, and then wrap with some final thoughts.

**TLDR: Spent the last couple of days in Dallas hanging out with bitcoiners, eating some good Texas food, and paying for my meals with Lightning.**

**Also, I finally had Steak ’n Shake for the first time!**

***

## The Amtrak Train

![](https://m.stacker.news/166330)

I actually took a train ride to Dallas from Austin, it was a very enjoyable ride I was able to get some work done and jump on a meeting too but the WiFi was spotty in the train so I just switched to my hotspot.

It was pretty comfortable not that many people were on it so it was the perfectly good type of quiet.

![](https://plebtv.com/m/pml_LhacfrdG_KwnmPbXR1MLUqQzT-psTRmV.mp4)

[Said](https://stacker.news/items/1613094?commentId=1613424) this in the saloon but central Texas is really beautiful this time of year, has a majestic feeling to it, indescribable in words tbh.

## First stop: Dallas Bitcoin Meetup

![](https://m.stacker.news/166319)

I attended the Dallas Bitcoin Meetup at Dunston’s Steak House. That’s not it lol that’s just a photo I took on the train, I was making my way through downtown Dallas, this beautiful old red courthouse caught my attention, just look at it, quite an achievement in building.

Apparently it’s built in 1892, it almost looks like a [medieval times](https://www.medievaltimes.com) type castle but real with its red sandstone, pointed rooftops and a clock tower!

Definitely had a moment of realization just how everyone arriving by this same train tracks for over a century probably felt the same way. Also something about seeing a building like this surrounded by modern skyscrapers that makes you appreciate the craftsmanship of another era.

So ya back to the meetup, so they’ve been getting together once a month, and I have to say, Dallas has a really good crew of bitcoiners and talk about the best place to do a meetup a Texas Steakhouse! 🤠

We started the evening with dinner before heading into a private room for presentations. That was actually such a great thing to do as well because most people can talk, chat and catch up since they last saw each other then move into the meetup for discussion, with more people just attending that in a separate room outside the dining area, was a pretty great experience tbh, and some of us in Austin should consider doing ahead of our meetups. 

The setup was smart because the coolest part is it made the meetup from 5pm till about 9:30pm and most people got there around 5ish to eat before the meetup at which point the presentations started at around 7pm where everyone else showed up.

The room was packed. The hospitality was amazing, the Bitcoiners there were very lovely people to talk with answer questions about Bitcoin startups and the AI wave were all experiencing. 

They asked me so many questions about AI x Lightning and did my best to answer them all. I found out later that a whole new group showed up for this one. So they could be growing as a community or maybe just curious about PlebLab in Austin as a lot of OG’s up there know about us.

I’ll admit something. I was a little nervous going into it. Which is funny because I talk to people for a living, between PlebLab, SNL, and all the events we put together in Austin, you would think I’d be used to it by now.

But there were a lot of people in that room I respect, and for whatever reason, I felt a nervous feeling right before.

![](https://m.stacker.news/166318)

My talk was about PlebLab, AI x Lightning, what we’ve been doing in 2026, what we’re building in the lab and where we’re going next in 2027 as a company. Lots of people came up afterwards thanking us for our hard work in Austin, I let them know we aren’t stopping till hyperbitcoinization.

The last presenter gave a really interesting presentation on multisig and entropy. I enjoyed that one quite a bit, that was one of coolest guys to meet, such a blast to talk too, as he talked about a lot of the great work D++ him and a group of others were doing around this to solve for the RNG bug they experienced with CC.

That’s the good wholesome stuff I love about local Bitcoin meetups. You can have conversations about startups, building communities or starting lightning projects, then spend the next hour getting into the weeds of private keys, entropy, and self-custody solutions discussing tradeoffs while everyone in the room genuinely cares.

![](https://m.stacker.news/166320)

One of the coolest parts of the evening happened when it was time to pay.

44,678 sats. I paid with Bitcoin on a Square terminal. Straight up Bitcoin Lightning baby, was awesome!

The waitress did ask if I needed to sign anything I told her no Bitcoin Lightning has instant settlement, no chargebacks or waiting for banks, she like that answer. 🤠

Overall I had an awesome night at the meetup got asked about a lot of things happening in Austin and what everyone is building, also got asked the usual do you know @supertestnet 😂 and I love it every time, he’s always the guy people bring up to me when I say I’m from PlebLab, someone also asked me about his songs and who recorded them, I said he did and yes that’s him really singing! Can you believe it! They said they couldn’t.🤣

## My first Steak ’n Shake

The next day, a bunch of us met up again at the Steak ’n Shake on Preston Road in Frisco.

Many of the same faces from the night before showed up. I was shocked not because they showed up but just because you can feel how much fun they enjoyed talking about Bitcoin and enjoying each others company.

Now, I’ve never actually eaten at Steak ’n Shake before. We don’t have one in Austin, although they’ve got locations in Dallas and San Antonio.

So I was pretty excited to finally try it.

![](https://m.stacker.news/166322)

Walking inside, the first thing that caught my attention was the big gold sign behind the counter.

**GRASS-FED & WAGYU**

Right underneath it:

**100% BEEF TALLOW**

I had to laugh it was like they were reading my mind. Between the grassfed beef, beef tallow fries, and Bitcoin payments, they certainly know how to get a our attention.

The whole place has this old school American diner feeling I was waiting for [Guy Fieri](https://watch.foodnetwork.com/show/diners-drive-ins-and-dives-food-network?xp=dds-atve__show_watchon_diners-drive-ins-and-dives) to come around the back. 

Red counters, black and white tile floors, and a pretty straightforward menu, it was true to itself, I love when brands do that!

![](https://m.stacker.news/166323)

You order everything through a touchscreen kiosk, and right there on the payment screen it says:

> Debit & Credit, Gift card and Bitcoin.

That’s it, just a terminal with choices it was so easy and simple.

Honestly was the best Lightning flow I’ve ever seen in my life, would argue it’s faster then paying tap2pay.👌

If you work on payments in Bitcoin Lightning and you haven’t experienced this flow you should, this is the correct way…*it felt so normal and futuristic.*

**Bitcoin Burger called the Steaktoshi**

![](https://m.stacker.news/166325)

For my first visit, I went with the Bitcoin Double Steakburger combo, supersized the fries to chili cheese fries, and grabbed a large drink.

The total came out to **$18.19.**

I paid **26,361 sats over Lightning.**

The payment was fast, the receipt printed, and nobody working there acted like I had just done something unusual.

Which, when you think about it, is exactly what we should want.

## ⚡️ 26,361 sats later

One thing I really liked was the receipt.

It showed the exchange rate at the time:

**1 USD = 1,449.16 sats**

It also had **Steaktoshi** printed on it, mentioned that the payment was powered by Fold, and even included an offer for a $5 Bitcoin gift card, feel free to take it if you want it stackers.

![](https://m.stacker.news/166351)

Little details like that are pretty cool.

I remember when paying for something with Bitcoin meant hoping the merchant’s wallet was working, explaining to someone what a QR code was, or waiting around for a payment to confirm.

Now I’m standing in a Steak ’n Shake ordering a burger like anybody else.

And the best part?

They stamp a giant ₿ right onto your burger bun. That genuinely made me laugh. 🤣 The person I was with said I looked giddy the whole time…yes I was!

![](https://m.stacker.news/166352)

The burger was good, the chili cheese fries were an experience on their own, and I throughly enjoyed the whole experience.

But what stood out more than anything was the customer service. Everyone working there was super nice!

We ended up talking with a guy named Adam who helped us out. He shared a little about what it’s been like receiving part of his wages in Bitcoin.

As a sn community we spend so much time talking about merchant adoption, payment infrastructure, and getting businesses to accept Bitcoin, that sometimes we forget about the people on the other side of those transactions, you can tell Adam thought it was cool too!

Adam said I could mention his name, so thanks again, Adam. Really appreciated the hospitality!

***

## The Good

I think what I enjoyed most about these two days wasn’t necessarily the payments themselves.

It was being around good wholesome people, I’m a sucker for that, and one of the many reasons I love going to church.

The night before, last night I was sitting in a room full of bitcoiners talking about self-custody, building projects that turn into companies, and the future of Bitcoin, I mean how cool is that!

The next afternoon, I was eating a burger with some of those same people, paying and slinging Lightning, and having a conversation with someone who earns part of his paycheck in sats, I mean how cool is that!

Two meals. Two Lightning payments. Not once did I have to explain what Bitcoin was. There’s something pretty remarkable about that, wasn’t always this way. Especially in places outside of Austin.

I’ve spent years talking about what Bitcoin adoption might look like. Sometimes it was easy for me to get lost in the arguments, bearish takes, fighting 💩coiners, and how everything is doom and gloom on the internet.

Then you go out into the real world, spend time with other bitcoiners, and realize that some of the things we’ve been talking about for years are quietly becoming normal and real world infrastructure all around you.

***

## Final Thoughts

You can spend all day on Stacker News, Nostr, or X talking about Bitcoin, but there’s still something special about sitting across the table from someone, sharing a meal, and getting to know the people who are actually using the things we all collectively build, it makes their life very enjoyable and we should all pick our heads up and see how much progress we’ve made collectively.

Anyway, if you’re in Dallas or Frisco, go get yourself a burger at Steak ’n Shake and pay with some sats.

And if you ever have the opportunity to attend the Dallas Bitcoin Meetup, I highly recommend it. Really good people doing some really good things in their community.

\*Question for you stackers I would love to hear about some of your favorite places to spend sats in the real world and how normal it’s become?\*

items.title: Always buy 2 pairs of eyeglasses
items.text: If you have to use eyeglasses, like anything they wear out. Just had to retire my first pair and on to the second this morning. Normally they last about 2-3 years before a new prescription is needed, but the first pair can wear out from regular, daily use. Having a second pair ready to go and new gives you a bump in vision with brand new, clear lenses and you don't have to stress about spending money months before a new prescription is likely going to happen. Usually a 2-fer is discounted to sell the eyeglasses. I always get mine at Costco as a pair.

items.title: The Billionaire Bankrolling of New, Physical Print Magazines
items.text:
Over five years ago, I wrote a piece called "[An Age of Patronage](https://thedailyeconomy.org/article/an-age-of-patronage/)" where I speculated how arts and research will/may work in a free world.

Basically sketching out the "value-for-value" revolution before that was cute or Lightning worked well enough for it.

## This month, I saw THREE print magazines launching/returning

**FIRST:** @asanoha and Bitcoin Art Magazine /Edition One https://stacker.news/items/1604664
This one isn't *quite* like the others -- for instance, I doubt there's a billionaire bankrolling it? -- but it's still a bet on a return to slow-form PHYSICAL MAGAZINES.

Definitely in the age of quick-hit/fast and hot takes AI slop, there's some.
Scarcity works like that, too: facing infinite generation, only the physical and human become scarce (https://stacker.news/items/1603955, https://stacker.news/items/1608788, https://stacker.news/items/1604664)

**SECOND:** LIFE magazine, a mainstay of 20th-century America, [is back](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/28/business/media/life-magazine-karlie-kloss.html). From that NYT article:

> The iconic magazine, known for its red-box logo and devotion to visual storytelling, will start publishing again next month as a quarterly print magazine.

*This*:

> It enters a fractured media landscape that is worlds away from the publication’s midcentury heights of acclaim, before the internet, social media and artificial intelligence upended the business model of magazine publishing.
> Daniel Okrent, who was the editor of Life magazine from 1992 to 1996, said that despite the value of the Life logo and the quality of the content, it was “a constantly unprofitable magazine” throughout history.

Also: run as a passion project/vanity thing for [small-time millionaire](https://www.celebritynetworth.com/richest-celebrities/models/karlie-kloss-net-worth/) and supermodel Karlie Kloss. Ruins Den's billionaire trend? No: husband is a [multibillionaire](https://www.eonline.com/news/1434962/inside-billionaire-josh-kushner-karlie-kloss-private-world). Funzies.

Also, importantly: NOT littered with ads. (Makes sense, since ad revenue isn't bankrolling them ANYWAY)

> The issue will come out on Nov. 23 as a large-format, 250-page print magazine retailing for $45, combining news photography with long-form journalism. There are no traditional print ads; instead the first issue is sponsored by Rivian and Figma.

says Wikipedia for why it closed its doors 25 years ago:

![](https://m.stacker.news/165194)

***

**THIRD:** Works in Progress.

Been seeing this a lot in my feed in recent weeks. (I imagine the algos heavily favor something you've visited/searched for recently) https://stacker.news/items/1591235, https://stacker.news/items/1598977, https://stacker.news/items/1601320

https://x.com/WorksInProgMag/status/2115617294005284869

No slop, *craft* in making beautiful things -- *and* important content.

The entire project is bankrolled by Stripe // Stripe Publishing and ultimate *their*owners, Patrick and John Collison et al.

***

It's *very* interesting to see this semi-/fake-capitalistic development, with art and storytelling and journalism be portrayed and worked on passionately by REAL and SERIOUS people, that looks and behaves like any other capitalist enterprise -- just *won't* be profit-oriented or ever aspire to making a profit.

## They're in it for the tech...

or rather, the humanity of it. The changing society. The craft and beauty and *deep meaning*.

I live this trend. And apparently, *sic semper salvatores*:

https://x.com/CharlesCMann/status/2118334333782012086

## All successful journalistic efforts were similarly "bankrolled by wealthy eccentrics"?

Yeah, I dunno. *But what did the rich ever do for us?!*

The recent anti-billionaire campaigns channeled their energy incorrectly. It's not that [the "rich" need to finance](https://thedailyeconomy.org/article/an-age-of-patronage/) failing programs like Medicare, or fat, lazy Californians' health problems. They should just build shit, bankroll artists, be \_patrons\_ to us creative peeps... and churches and architecture and all the other beautiful things in human/western civ. 

## "patronage is “the tribute which opulence owes to genius.” --Edmund Burke

> If you were wealthy, **it was your moral obligation to give back to the community** – not merely by improving the lot of the poor or renovating your local church but also by supporting artists and intellectuals.

Interesting future ahead of us. Huuuuge if true.

items.title: Chess improvement -- kill the mid-wit and find the elusive "spirit of chess"
items.text:
I was recently watching this [Chess Vibes video](https://www.youtube.com/live/zp0oiZGWRYw), where he tries to coach a ~1200 elo (presumably) adult improver, commenting on his games as he plays, and to use a Christian term, felt mildly *convicted* as I watched, as SpaceVega's sins reflected my own back to me. 

SpaceVega played beautiful openings. Actually watching some of his early Caro-Kann games, and how effortlessly he made it look to getting a really nice position, got me thinking I want to play that opening, and had me watching through [Eric Hansen's excellent run](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLUjxDD7HNNTjVEZ_1I8E28uav9t_ltDKX&si=wi3M2Ayt9WtTTJKy). 

(I have played the French, for my sins, and the Caro-Kann just looked like a more OP version, as SpaceVega would get the "bad" LSB out early and use it to wreck his opponent's pawn structure. But, really, Dash, you need to learn yet *another* opening? Is that going to help you stop hanging mate in one? Or playing unsound sacrifices?)

As I watched SpaceVega play more and more, get a great position out of the opening, then missing tactic after tactic, and eventually losing, or winning despite his best efforts to throw the game, making life hard for himself with poor conversion technique, it brought to mind an observation that I made about myself, and other adult improvers, that we often just focus on the *wrong* things (*cough* openings) when trying to improve at chess. 

I think one reason for this is that as adults drawn to chess, we are often attracted to the aesthetics of the game. We like the look of a nice position. We like to win with an opening trap in 9 moves and feel smart. We like to spend 100 or 1000s of dollars on opening courses, convincing ourselves that *just one more course* will finally propel us to our "true" rating. 

And what don't we like? Complications. Calculation. *Fighting*. Uncertainty. We don't like when a "pawn pusher" breaks all the opening principles and steamrolls our expensive London system "unfairly". We don't like time pressure. We just want to be left alone to recall our favorite lines and play in peace. 

And what about kids? You know, who are playing the game to have *fun* instead of attaching their fragile self-worth to a matching-algorithm number. Kids love *tactics*. They love forks. The love knights. They never miss a skewer. The strike at any tactical opportunity like a coiled snake. No sooner have you pushed your sweatily considered queen move when your vertically challenged antagonist has forked you with some bishop move. Instantly. Not even the courtesy to think about it first. 

Because chess is about *thinking* right? You go through your mental check list. You consider the *principles* of the game. What did Silman say about open files? That knight looks dangerous, but Ben Finegold told me never to push my f pawn.... You spend 5 mins on a move, recalling every book, every YouTube video, every Chessable course, meanwhile the kid just sees the tactic and takes your lady. 

Philidor said that "paws are the souls of chess". I think that "tactics are the spirit of chess". And I know, every beginner gets told to work on their tactics. This is not anything new or particularly interesting. But I think it's worth thinking about *why* tactics are so important when improving at chess. 

Because just like I think Silman's books are about thinking and fighting, and not really about "imbalances", I think tactics are about the "spirit of chess", which is to say, honing the instinct to pounce on your opponent's mistakes with a ruthless intensity. You need to somehow foster this mindset, or perhaps "mushin/ non-mind" as the Japanese martial artists may have described it. And that's going to take a lot of practice and pattern recognition. But more than anything, it's about backing yourself, trusting you calculation, and trying to get over the adult mid-wit fear of "what if I miss something?" which causes you to overthink, hesitate, or seek protection through the safety of the known, in excessive study of opening theory. 

It's like, you need to play chess to actually *play* chess, in order to get better at chess, if that makes sense. 
Maybe nonsense. Maybe there is just a hard limit related to biological determinism and the idea of chess improvement beyond a certain point is just alchemy. But some arbitrary pursuit of arcane knowledge/ secret wisdom is needed to keep the civilized mind occupied. May as well be chess. At least, it keeps me away from conspiracy theories and politics.

items.title: OpenBitcoin.com: A new bitcoin block explorer with guides tools and games
items.text:
I have been building a bitcoin block explorer and I feel it's good enough to show:

[https://openbitcoin.com](https://openbitcoin.com)

The site runs its own hardware, bitcoin node and address index. No third-party blockchain API used.

Inside the site:

- Explorer: blocks, transactions and addresses at root-level URLs. (very important, a feature I always wanted with other explorers, a quick easy way to query an address) For example you can type openbitcoin.com/block_number_here or openbitcoin.com/txid_here or openbitcoin.com/address_here to load the page instantly without visiting the site to use the search bar :)

- Node census (openbitcoin.com/nodes): reachable nodes counted by my own P2P crawler, 8,958 nodes from 92 countries last run.

- Rich list (openbitcoin.com/rich-list): top 10,000 addresses and balance distributions.

- Prices: spot price as a median of three exchanges, with a quick conversion tool on the front page.

- Tools: fee calculator, address validator, message verifier, QR generator, and key tools built to be downloaded and run offline.

- Guides: on confirmations, UTXOs, self-custody, stuck transactions and more. Newbie friendly.

- Games (openbitcoin.com/games): three arcade games built on real bitcoin mechanics, stack blocks, clear a mempool backlog, and a slot machine that plays the actual odds of guessing a private key.

The website is open source. What stays private is my server's operational layer.

Would appreciate any feedback, happy to contribute to the community.

items.title: [Read-along] The Odyssey, W.H.D. Rouse, Books IV - VI
items.text:
*If you've been following along--catch up on the last* [part](https://stacker.news/items/1595925/r/billytheked)*--you probably have found this to be a relaxed pace of reading. Maybe more so than you wish. Alas, life has way of keeping me from this project. As mentioned before, I am reading a hard copy of the translation of W.H.D. Rouse, but I can also recommend the* [*digitized version of the translation of A.S. Kline.*](https://www.poetryintranslation.com/PITBR/Greek/Odhome.php)

***

In the next three books, finally we meet Odysseus, who is (reluctantly?) biding his time on some island with a nymph named Calypso. We hear from his peer, Menelaos and Helen, how Odysseus' heroism and restraint delivered them to victory against the Trojans; however, it becomes harder to distinguish who the true Odysseus really is. His tendency to appear differently from his true nature begins to reveal itself in the stories told about him, and now, first hand, as we are taken along on his adventure to meet the Phaiacians. Thus, we begin to find some truth in the first line of the poem, as translated W.H.D. Rouse, 'here is the story of a man who is never at a loss.' Odysseus begins to earn the name he bears (ὀδύσσομα), whose meaning in Greek translates into something like "to be hated."

## Discussion on Themes

**Hospitality**
The vivid descriptions of feasting, drinking, and making sacrifice to the gods upon the arrival of a guests has defined the escapades of Telemachos up to book IV in the poem. Even as he goes to the house of Menelaos, his good manners and refined appearance precede him, even before he has the chance to make himself known as the son of Odysseus. The Odyssey, being the "national" epic of the Achaeans, takes painstaking effort to provide encyclopedic, lurid descriptions of the level of civilization that had been achieved by Greeks at that time. Clearly, the poem paints a complete and detailed picture of their cultural achievement in the deeply entrenched and refined mores that consistently define what it meant to be Greek. This cultural consistency stands in contrast to the geographic and political separation of the different kingdoms that existed at the time.

**Appearances versus reality**
Finally, in Book V, the reader gets their introduction to Odysseus, who, despite his loyalty to his wife, is on some island playing house with the Nymph Calypso. Since Odysseus rarely presents himself as he truly is, it is impossible for the reader to differentiate whether his desire to return home is authentic, or some hollowed-out sense of moral duty. The reader first learns of his duplicity when Helen recounts how he sneaked into Troy disguised as a beggar, revealing to her their plans to sack the Trojans and rescue her. Also, when Calypso, tells Odysseus he can return home as long as he concedes that his wife is not prettier than her, he lays with her, and doesn't resist. Again, as Odysseus approaches Nausicaa in book VI, he appears as a homeless beggar, in want of proper clothes, when in fact, as we know, Odysseus is the center of attention on Mt Olympus.

**The sea/landscape both as friend and enemy**
There is this sense in the poem that the god of the sea, Earthshaker Poseidon, is the single chaotic force that the Achaeans owe their greatness to, as well as their woes. Nausicaa says to her maids that there is no mortal enemy who do harm on Phaiacia since their country is out of reach, "far away at sea." Also, despite Zeus and Athena's desire to see Odysseus return home, it is grumpy old Poseidon who hurls continued misfortune upon him, as seen after he leaves Calypso. The poem uses the "wine-darkened" sea as a representation of a kind of frontier of civilization, acting at the same time as a buffer of defense, but also a liminal and chaotic realm, where just about anything can happen.

## Questions for contemplation

* **How do you define the frontier of civilization now? Is it a physical place/thing, technological, or something else?**
* **What American national epics document the height of its culture and civilization? How would you characterize these works?**
* **In your opinion, how should we read Odysseus' trickery, as a mark of virtue or a vice?**

# Summaries

## Book IV

Menelaos recounts the death of his brother, Agememnon and laments Odysseus' apparent death, not knowing that he is talking to the latter's very own son. Helen of Troy sedates everyone present with some kind of drug she picked up in Egypt, and tells them the story Odysseus in Troy, where Helen, being held captive, recognized Odysseus disguised as a beggar, who was able to tell her of the Greek's plan to sack the city. Menelaos recounts how he heard her as she circled and touched the Trojan horse, calling our his name, and that if it weren't for Odysseus's being there, urging restraint, he would have called back, blowing their cover. He then tells the story of how he tricked the Old Man of the Sea in Egypt, disguising himself and two of his men with seal carcasses so they can ambush him while he is asleep. The Old Man tells Menelaos of Agememnon's murder, and how Odysseus was still living. Penelope, back in Ithica, prays to Athena, as her suitors plot against Telemachos, laying in wait for his ships to return. Athena summons the ghost of Iphthime, daughter of Icarus, to visit Athena in her sleep to inform her that she will protect Telemachos from harm.

## Book V

Zeus and Athena discuss Odysseus' fate. Zeus reluctantly agrees to intervene to by sending Hermes to inform Calypso of their desire to see Odysseus find his way home, on the condition that Odysseus travel without man or god, and only after a good dose of bad fortune. Calpyso tells Hermes that she loves Odysseus, but does not wish to anger Zeus. She tells Odysseus that it is the god's will that he be allowed to go home, but that he must admit she is prettier than his wife, which he does, and the sleeps with her. Calypso send him off, helping him to hew trees and craft a ship, supplies him with food and wine and water. Poseidon sees Odysseus thus returning, close to his destiny, and decides on shaking up his world, sending a storm his way, to throw him off course. Ino, or Leucothea, the White Sea Goddess, takes pity on him, orders him to strip his clothes and gives him a veil that helps him swim to safety. At first Odysseus refuses, choosing to test his fate and his trusted raft, but this quickly shatters like straw on the threshing floor, and he takes Ino's advice. After he swims to safety, he kisses the earth, returns the veil to Ino, prays to Zeus, and finds a place to take shelter, collapsing from exhaustion.

## Book VI

In the house of Alcinoos, king of the Phaiacians, sleeps his daughter, Nausicaa. Athena visits her in a dream to inspire her to take all of her best bridal linens down to the river to be washed, for the time is coming when she must be prepared to be wed. Thus, Nausicaa appeals to her father, who allows this, prepares for her carts and donkeys. She and her maids take the linens down to a rushing stream, bathe, lather in olive oil, and adorn themselves as the goddess Artemis, daughter of Zeus. They begin playing ball, when Athena decides that it is time that Odysseus is awaken. She causes one of them to drop the ball, sending it hurling down toward the eddies, awakening him. He emerges, craggy and briny, approaches the women, all who get scared away except for Nausicaa, whose fear Athena removed. Odysseus, impressed by her refinement, makes an appeal to her for clothes, which she agrees to. He washes and changes, and Athena makes him taller and more handsome. Finally, the latter invites Odysseus to return to Phaiacia among her party, instructing him to hide in her father's orchard until she makes it back to her father's house. She gives him instructions on how to find her, and tells him he must supplicate himself to her mother if he wishes to return to his own people.

items.title: [Sauna Shorts] 21 Futures: Behemoth
items.text:
My last sauna read was the third chapter from 21 Futures, titled Behemoth.

The setting is an O'Neil Cylinder in deep space. We follow two kids who are eagerly racing off to see an enormous ship, The Behemoth, from Earth. It has real Earthers on it! The kids seldom if ever see people from Earth and are taken by the short stature and funny garb of these gravitationally stunted people.

They go check out a shop and are disappointed that their allowance of 500 msats is not enough to buy any of the cool stuff from Earth, like books with real paper. The annoyed shop keeper directs them towards a discount bin of crap he hasn't been able to unload. They can't even afford most of the junk but have fun dinking around with the old tech. 

Eventually, there's a chase related to the kids discovering an ancient storage device with 0.25 BTC on it. To say that's generational wealth is a vast understatement. This is like own your own space station wealth in the distant future. 

I loved this idea and the setting. I'm a huge nerd for space colonization stuff. I hadn't really thought about how all these BTC storage devices might turn into the buried treasure of the future, but it's a very romantic idea.

items.title: Paolo got sick
items.text:
Yesterday morning, Paolo got me worried. Anyone who has pets can tell when something isn't right. He was a bit sluggish, sleepy, had gone 12 hours without using the litter box, and didn't have much of an appetite. He climbed onto my lap looking for affection, and I noticed he had an ear injury that isn't visible at first glance. His eye infection also came back, the exact same one he had when he first arrived at our home. On top of this, he had been having stomach issues; 3 or 4 days ago, he threw up all his food right after eating, and his stools haven't been healthy. Just a few days ago, he was his usual self active, playful, acting like the king of the house.

![](https://m.stacker.news/165807)

I borrowed some money and took him to the vet. She is a doctor with a wonderful heart for animals and had tremendous patience; the appointment lasted about an hour. She prescribed several medications:

For his eye: Antibiotic eye drops and artificial tears.For the ear injury: An antiseptic solution to clean it and a healing cream.

She ordered stool tests and prescribed dewormer, antifungal medication, probiotics, a nutritional supplement for cats with deficiencies, and "gastrointestinal wet food," which I researched and found out is medicated food specifically for gastrointestinal conditions.

Paolo isn't used to riding in cars, so he was scared and started panting on the way back home.

![](https://m.stacker.news/165813)

Use a basket and its blanket to transport it.

Today I got his stool analysis done. No parasites showed up, though the vet said she found it strange and asked me to bring another sample to her clinic so she can send it to a different lab (she isn't charging me for this). What the test did show is that he has intestinal dysbiosis.

The hardest part for me is affording all his medications, especially the special food he was prescribed, because each can costs $12 and only lasts him one day.

I already bought one of the medications, Itraconazole, and I still need to get the rest. The doctor said that once he gets better, he can switch to dry food (a higher quality brand, which costs around $30 for a 2kg bag that lasts a month) along with homemade food.

Paolo's treatment is costing me 70% of my income (not even counting the special food). I am reaching out to this community and fellow cat lovers to ask if you could help me heal Paolo.

items.title: A Lodging for Wayfaring Men Book Club: Covetousness and Revaluing the Self
items.text:
*Welcome to the seventh week of our book club reading* A Lodging for Wayfaring Men. *We're reading one chapter every two weeks, so we'll be discussing Chapter 4 next Saturday, but in between-weeks we are having a look at the essays in Appendix A. They are short and accessible.*

*You can find the book club reading schedule here:* https://stacker.news/items/1582413

---

# Covetousness and Revaluing the Self by Prester John

At first, I thought this essay was a little woo-woo, new age, but having thought about it for a while, perhaps there is something here. Certainly, this repositioning of "covetousness" is interesting:

> People who conceive of themselves as worthy of good things, valuable of themselves, deserving and expectant of pleasure, are not covetous, since *covetousness presupposes that you cannot get what you want by your own virtues, and must seize it by fraud.*

When we bump up against covetousness, it's often, as Prester John says in this essay, something like envy -- it's all about things that are external to us. Prester John revereses it and makes covetousness all about our own opinion of ourselves -- and especially what we think we are capable of. 

# "Do you think that you have the ability to create what you want to out of life?"

A word I've been seeing a lot lately in Bitcoin is "sovereignty." It seems like the Bitcoiners who want to pivot to AI but feel sheepish about it are rebranding under "sovereignty" as a way of making it seem like they have not given up on Bitcoin. Nevertheless, sovereignty seems very close to what Prester John is talking about with taking yourself seriously enough that you believe you can create the things you want in life. This is very compelling -- especially now as it seems that AI tools can be used to solve so much of the friction that may have given people reason to give up in the past. 

But, a problem with this sort of thinking is this: what if you want more than you are capable of achieving?

> No, having devalued your self is not your fault. We were all born into this. These ideas have pervaded all generations and groups of men throughout recorded history. We learned it from our parents and associates, who learned it from theirs. But though it is not your fault, it remains your problem to fix.

If this is the case, I want to know why. why should humanity have developed this way and not along some more honest, noble -- and according to Prester John -- more accurate vision of itself? Because, unless there's a good explanation for that, it seems like we are unlikely to change it.

I've been reading Ursula K LeGuin's *The Dispossessed* lately. In that story, there are two societies -- a decadent, stratified society much like ours and a noble, anarchic society on the moon above them. The people from this anarchic society seem to have none of the cultural hangups that the more earthly society groans beneath -- and when a scientist from the anarchic society comes down to earth, he is disconcerted by interactions with servants and people in the lower classes -- people who don't seem to mind being treated as servants.

I don't think there are very many people in the world who are uninteresting and have no dreams -- even if most dreams get abandoned in the face of life's many obstacles. But I think what Prester John is getting at is that most of us have pretty severe constraints placed on our dreams -- and we don't often take time to evaluate these. 

> The solution is to revalue yourself. This does not mean that you should become arrogant and fake. It means that you should analyze your own self-image, and refuse to act on a low or negative estimation of yourself. This will be slow process, and difficult at times.

Well, of course we should, but then there's all these guy wires holding us down. You try to free up your estimation of yourself but you've still got to provide for a family, pay for insurance, it won't do to abandon your friendships, and each one of these is a small enough force on its own, but together they make up a rats nest of responsibilities that prevent you from really changing very much about this estimation of yourself. After all, guy wires are there to stabilize things, even if they end up holding it down. 

# So, if Prester John is right, and we live in a society that -- for whatever reason -- has crippled our dreaming organs, what do you think you would dream of if you able?

---

# Covetousness and Revaluing the Self by Prester John

During my years as a rabid follower of Jesus, I spent a lot of time going over Bible texts. (And I do mean a lot of time.) Even though I no longer think that those texts were inspired by an omnipotent creator, I do recognize that they were written by a lot of very insightful guys, who, if not always finding the right answers, were at least asking the right questions. One of the things I discovered in my studies was the real meaning and significance of covetousness.

Covetousness is one of those old words that was little-understood even in the old days. Most people think it meant something like envy. But that falls significantly short of the real meaning.

Covetousness has to do with something deeper, with valuing ourselves. Do you think that you have the ability to create what you want to out of life? Now, I’m not asking you if you have actually done this. We all know that the world is fraught with traps, difficulties, and sometimes insurmountable obstacles. But, if those obstacles didn’t exist, would you have the built-in ability to create what you want?

Let me provide some background on this by giving you a very literal translation of a passage from the Bible (Ephesians) that seems to refer to what happened after the famed episode in the garden of Eden, beginning just after man was ejected:

“They went plodding through life in the ineffectiveness of their consciousness. The stream of their consciousness was dimmed by the solidification and desensitizing of their core. And so, they became non-participants in the divine life. This hurt them so badly that they became apathetic, and in that state, gave up control of themselves, and toiled in a reverse catharsis, with covetousness.” The exact rendering of the word “covetousness” here would be “more-hold.” That is, they sought to hold more than they had created on their own. By wanting to hold on to more than you’ve made, you are judging yourself as incapable of making it yourself.

People who conceive of themselves as worthy of good things, valuable of themselves, deserving and expectant of pleasure, are not covetous, since *covetousness presupposes that you cannot get what you want by your own virtues, and must seize it by fraud.*

Thus, when you sell out (reach a point where the money is good enough for you to sell your honor), you are naming your own value. Perceiving yourself to be unable to create what you want by your own virtues, you sell out.

This finds application in myriad ways.

The point of this discussion is that all humans of our era must fight to revalue themselves. All of us have been touched by covetousness in one way or another (probably in many, many ways), and have accepted a devalued self-estimation. (There’s another very interesting Bible passage that literally translated says “according to your estimation, it happens unto you.”)

No, having devalued your self is not your fault. We were all born into this. These ideas have pervaded all generations and groups of men throughout recorded history. We learned it from our parents and associates, who learned it from theirs. But though it is not your fault, it remains your problem to fix.

The solution is to revalue yourself. This does not mean that you should become arrogant and fake. It means that you should analyze your own self-image, and refuse to act on a low or negative estimation of yourself. This will be slow process, and difficult at times.

By virtue of being a living human, you have immense capabilities. Yes, there may be difficult, or even impossible, obstacles in front of you; but that does not change your basic abilities – they are there, and are more powerful than we have understood.

Remember that sacrificing truth and honor to what seems immediately necessary is based upon either a low estimation of yourself, or – only occasionally – upon truly impossible obstacles.

Work on it. It’ll take time, but work on it.

items.title: [Cantill One – play central banker] First multiplayer world open!
items.text:
I've been building Cantill One, a browser game about money. You run a country with its own currency: interest rate, taxes, spending, tariffs, and your money system (fiat, gold, fixed supply or a Bitcoin standard). Print too much and you get the Cantillon effect. New money reaches the banker first and the low earner last, bubbles grow, and some day they burst.

Tonight the first persistent world opened:

- 24 countries, run by the AI until people take them over
- 1 game month = 1 real hour, and time keeps running when you're offline
- Build infrastructure, ports, gold vaults… and watch them turn into ruins when your bubble bursts
- Form unions, start tariff wars, and survive an election every 4 game years (every 2 days)
- The best currency wins, measured by how well its people actually live

This first world is a **test run** with no prize, and it lasts 8 days. **Everyone who plays it gets a whitelist spot for the first world with a sats prize pool.**
Turn on 🔔 in the game and it pings you when a building slot frees up, before your election, or when things go wrong.

Missed the earlier single player challenges? Here they are:
- I made a game where you play central banker. Today's winner gets 10k sats ⚡ (https://stacker.news/items/1601648)
- Nixon Shock 1971 challenge – 48h, 50k prize pool ⚡ (https://stacker.news/items/1605580)

👉 https://cantill.one

Feedback is very welcome, especially on pacing and whether you come back after a day.

items.title: [Total Chess Championship]: Anish Bringing the Homecooking, GOAT Almost Out
items.text:
Magnus, the world's #1 (for now...?) https://stacker.news/items/1614144 and the undisputed best chess player of the last two decades -- arguably *ever* -- is on the ropes. In the tournament *and* about to lose his spot as world #1 (https://stacker.news/items/1613921).

He had a great position against Shakh... and squandered it away for a draw. Trailing Anish by 6 points, with 9 points left to play for, he's not *entirely* out. (But it's not far off... we need some truly epic Magnesian magic)

Also, CRAZY checkmate-in-1 blunder in a TOTALLY winning position. [Rapport vs Pragg](https://www.chess.com/events/2026-total-chess-world-championship-tour-pilot-group-b/07/Rapport_Richard-Praggnanandhaa_R)... **look at that, you can hang checkmate-in-1, too; *just like a supergrandmaster!***

(https://stacker.news/items/1613515 https://stacker.news/items/1613935 https://stacker.news/items/1614144)

***

**Anish threw a barbecue with some home-cooked preparation** in some sort of English-by-transposition (https://stacker.news/items/1608022). On move #7, we go h4 -- *obviously*. This should come with a "kids, don't do this at home" warning... No development, no castling, just HURL PAWNS at your opponent.

![](https://m.stacker.news/166399)

...a few moves later, and the pawn is on h6. *Annoying!* And in the skirmish we get the funniest-looking white pawns of the day (maybe tournament??). Why *in the world* is there a pawn on f6?!

![](https://m.stacker.news/166401)

Anish hunts Mishra's king out into the open, who counterpunches by attacking the b1 rook with the bishop. Move it? Defend it? 

*Nah*, just sac it... *brilliance by castling, eh?*


![](https://m.stacker.news/166402)

My e2 bishop (together with the queen and dark-squared bishop already posed to jump in) is worth WAAAY more as an attacker than what you gain in material by snatching my rook.

Mishra, wisely, doesn't dare taking it. (And computer says that was the right choice...). On the next move, the bishop gets pinned to the king: no more free rook for yah. With all that stuff happening on the kingside, *you go and steamroll black in the middle of the board as well!* Sexy:

![](https://m.stacker.news/166405)

Maybe we should have titled this game "The Revenge of the Pawns."

Anish fibbled it a little, allowing Mishra back into the game and into an even-material rook-and-pawn endgame, snagged a pawn, and never looked back. Easy pickings.

![](https://m.stacker.news/166404)

It was +4 or +5 at some point, but elite grandmasters can manage it comfortably with +2.5/2.9 as well. NO WORRIES.

## Always invite Anish to your garden BBQ

News  

Welcome to Books & Articles Weekly.  Sorry I posted this a little late. I zapped the posts earlier. I really enjoyed this week's content. @Undisciplined 's 21 Futures reviews (where do you find the time and energy?) and the @Dash_1971 Neuromancer review are hopefully just the start of regular posting from these stackers.

 I hope you all have a good week.

Thanks to everyone who contributed.

There is a zap award for the top 5 posts weekly. It will be broken down as follows:

1. 1000 sats 
2.   250 sats
3.   250 sats 
4.   250 sats 
5.   250 sats


I choose the top 5 posts each week based on sats, engagement, and overall quality. The cut off time is 9:00am EST (1300GMT) Saturday morning. I will post the top 5 winners shortly around 9:00am every Saturday morning.

I reserve the right to not award any sats for the week. I also reserve the right to deny sat awards to bare link posts. I recognize that link posts can be valuable, so I will only exercise discretion for low quality links that garner few sats or engagement from stackers.


Happy reading!


As always, please reply with suggestions and opinions on how to make this territory better.

items.title: Don't try to change the Bitcoin protocol, make it irrelevant
items.text:
@btcplusplus published an excellent article by @AdamISZ (aka waxwing) today. In it, waxwing points out that when it comes to development on Bitcoin, it can seem like,

> The vast majority of active work is — rather like work in corporations — erudite work on the *details*

He goes on to provide a list of examples:

> complex mempool management like [TRUC](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0431.mediawiki) and the like; the extreme subtleties of better versions of multisig, backup, stealth addresses (now [Silent Payments](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0352.mediawiki)), coinswap; details of [payjoin](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0077.md) and other coinjoin variants; signature aggregation. Many of the ideas being refined are over a decade old.

I certainly resonate with this feeling. I haven't felt that it is necessarily a bad thing (nor a good thing) but it does seem like a pretty accurate description of what's going on in Bitcoin right now. It's a lot of reacting, not very much excitement.[^1]

[^1]: I'm sympathetic to the idea that Bitcoin doesn't need to be exciting. And perhaps I am using the wrong word in "excitement" -- what I mean to identify is the feeling that we somehow are not taking full advantage of money you can send to anyone, anywhere, anytime and no one can stop you.

# "So where does the revolutionary still exist?" 

> I claim it lives neither in trying to make changes to Bitcoin itself (new opcodes etc.), nor in editing the finer details of what already exists, but separate from all this: in *cryptography*.

On the one hand, this is a very exciting way to look at it: we have more computing power than ever at our disposal and the ability to do really wild things with math...on the other hand new cryptography is one of the scariest things I can think of. In this age of the constant discovery of vulnerabilities, I often use the fact that SHA256 is really really battle tested as my security blanket. 

Nonetheless, what waxwing says here has this advantage: it doesn't require permission. I'm not saying whatever can be done on bitcoin should be done, but at the least, I think we are better off if people are willing to try lots of wacky things (that don't require protocol changes). 

# "this is the revolutionary, cypherpunk idea: don’t try to overturn the institution; make it irrelevant. If Bitcoin is ossified, fine. So is TCP, for that matter. We work on a new level, a new paradigm."

> Don’t get lost in either the reactionary “take down the institution, smash it and build a virtuous new one”, or the “I will join the institution and work on some tiny corner of it for ten years, hoping for an incremental change”. Dare to dream a little bigger.

# What is the little bigger that we might dream?

Two Days in Dallas - Review
items.text:
## **Two Days in Dallas**

⚡️⚡️⚡️⚡️⚡️ 5/5 Zaps. Worth the visit if you can make the trek, one of my new favorite Bitcoin citys to visit, will be back again!

***

I’ll start with the places I went, move to the good, and then wrap with some final thoughts.

**TLDR: Spent the last couple of days in Dallas hanging out with bitcoiners, eating some good Texas food, and paying for my meals with Lightning.**

**Also, I finally had Steak ’n Shake for the first time!**

***

## The Amtrak Train

![](https://m.stacker.news/166330)

I actually took a train ride to Dallas from Austin, it was a very enjoyable ride I was able to get some work done and jump on a meeting too but the WiFi was spotty in the train so I just switched to my hotspot.

It was pretty comfortable not that many people were on it so it was the perfectly good type of quiet.

![](https://plebtv.com/m/pml_LhacfrdG_KwnmPbXR1MLUqQzT-psTRmV.mp4)

[Said](https://stacker.news/items/1613094?commentId=1613424) this in the saloon but central Texas is really beautiful this time of year, has a majestic feeling to it, indescribable in words tbh.

## First stop: Dallas Bitcoin Meetup

![](https://m.stacker.news/166319)

I attended the Dallas Bitcoin Meetup at Dunston’s Steak House. That’s not it lol that’s just a photo I took on the train, I was making my way through downtown Dallas, this beautiful old red courthouse caught my attention, just look at it, quite an achievement in building.

Apparently it’s built in 1892, it almost looks like a [medieval times](https://www.medievaltimes.com) type castle but real with its red sandstone, pointed rooftops and a clock tower!

Definitely had a moment of realization just how everyone arriving by this same train tracks for over a century probably felt the same way. Also something about seeing a building like this surrounded by modern skyscrapers that makes you appreciate the craftsmanship of another era.

So ya back to the meetup, so they’ve been getting together once a month, and I have to say, Dallas has a really good crew of bitcoiners and talk about the best place to do a meetup a Texas Steakhouse! 🤠

We started the evening with dinner before heading into a private room for presentations. That was actually such a great thing to do as well because most people can talk, chat and catch up since they last saw each other then move into the meetup for discussion, with more people just attending that in a separate room outside the dining area, was a pretty great experience tbh, and some of us in Austin should consider doing ahead of our meetups. 

The setup was smart because the coolest part is it made the meetup from 5pm till about 9:30pm and most people got there around 5ish to eat before the meetup at which point the presentations started at around 7pm where everyone else showed up.

The room was packed. The hospitality was amazing, the Bitcoiners there were very lovely people to talk with answer questions about Bitcoin startups and the AI wave were all experiencing. 

They asked me so many questions about AI x Lightning and did my best to answer them all. I found out later that a whole new group showed up for this one. So they could be growing as a community or maybe just curious about PlebLab in Austin as a lot of OG’s up there know about us.

I’ll admit something. I was a little nervous going into it. Which is funny because I talk to people for a living, between PlebLab, SNL, and all the events we put together in Austin, you would think I’d be used to it by now.

But there were a lot of people in that room I respect, and for whatever reason, I felt a nervous feeling right before.

![](https://m.stacker.news/166318)

My talk was about PlebLab, AI x Lightning, what we’ve been doing in 2026, what we’re building in the lab and where we’re going next in 2027 as a company. Lots of people came up afterwards thanking us for our hard work in Austin, I let them know we aren’t stopping till hyperbitcoinization.

The last presenter gave a really interesting presentation on multisig and entropy. I enjoyed that one quite a bit, that was one of coolest guys to meet, such a blast to talk too, as he talked about a lot of the great work D++ him and a group of others were doing around this to solve for the RNG bug they experienced with CC.

That’s the good wholesome stuff I love about local Bitcoin meetups. You can have conversations about startups, building communities or starting lightning projects, then spend the next hour getting into the weeds of private keys, entropy, and self-custody solutions discussing tradeoffs while everyone in the room genuinely cares.

![](https://m.stacker.news/166320)

One of the coolest parts of the evening happened when it was time to pay.

44,678 sats. I paid with Bitcoin on a Square terminal. Straight up Bitcoin Lightning baby, was awesome!

The waitress did ask if I needed to sign anything I told her no Bitcoin Lightning has instant settlement, no chargebacks or waiting for banks, she like that answer. 🤠

Overall I had an awesome night at the meetup got asked about a lot of things happening in Austin and what everyone is building, also got asked the usual do you know @supertestnet 😂 and I love it every time, he’s always the guy people bring up to me when I say I’m from PlebLab, someone also asked me about his songs and who recorded them, I said he did and yes that’s him really singing! Can you believe it! They said they couldn’t.🤣

## My first Steak ’n Shake

The next day, a bunch of us met up again at the Steak ’n Shake on Preston Road in Frisco.

Many of the same faces from the night before showed up. I was shocked not because they showed up but just because you can feel how much fun they enjoyed talking about Bitcoin and enjoying each others company.

Now, I’ve never actually eaten at Steak ’n Shake before. We don’t have one in Austin, although they’ve got locations in Dallas and San Antonio.

So I was pretty excited to finally try it.

![](https://m.stacker.news/166322)

Walking inside, the first thing that caught my attention was the big gold sign behind the counter.

**GRASS-FED & WAGYU**

Right underneath it:

**100% BEEF TALLOW**

I had to laugh it was like they were reading my mind. Between the grassfed beef, beef tallow fries, and Bitcoin payments, they certainly know how to get a our attention.

The whole place has this old school American diner feeling I was waiting for [Guy Fieri](https://watch.foodnetwork.com/show/diners-drive-ins-and-dives-food-network?xp=dds-atve__show_watchon_diners-drive-ins-and-dives) to come around the back. 

Red counters, black and white tile floors, and a pretty straightforward menu, it was true to itself, I love when brands do that!

![](https://m.stacker.news/166323)

You order everything through a touchscreen kiosk, and right there on the payment screen it says:

> Debit & Credit, Gift card and Bitcoin.

That’s it, just a terminal with choices it was so easy and simple.

Honestly was the best Lightning flow I’ve ever seen in my life, would argue it’s faster then paying tap2pay.👌

If you work on payments in Bitcoin Lightning and you haven’t experienced this flow you should, this is the correct way…*it felt so normal and futuristic.*

**Bitcoin Burger called the Steaktoshi**

![](https://m.stacker.news/166325)

For my first visit, I went with the Bitcoin Double Steakburger combo, supersized the fries to chili cheese fries, and grabbed a large drink.

The total came out to **$18.19.**

I paid **26,361 sats over Lightning.**

The payment was fast, the receipt printed, and nobody working there acted like I had just done something unusual.

Which, when you think about it, is exactly what we should want.

## ⚡️ 26,361 sats later

One thing I really liked was the receipt.

It showed the exchange rate at the time:

**1 USD = 1,449.16 sats**

It also had **Steaktoshi** printed on it, mentioned that the payment was powered by Fold, and even included an offer for a $5 Bitcoin gift card, feel free to take it if you want it stackers.

![](https://m.stacker.news/166351)

Little details like that are pretty cool.

I remember when paying for something with Bitcoin meant hoping the merchant’s wallet was working, explaining to someone what a QR code was, or waiting around for a payment to confirm.

Now I’m standing in a Steak ’n Shake ordering a burger like anybody else.

And the best part?

They stamp a giant ₿ right onto your burger bun. That genuinely made me laugh. 🤣 The person I was with said I looked giddy the whole time…yes I was!

![](https://m.stacker.news/166352)

The burger was good, the chili cheese fries were an experience on their own, and I throughly enjoyed the whole experience.

But what stood out more than anything was the customer service. Everyone working there was super nice!

We ended up talking with a guy named Adam who helped us out. He shared a little about what it’s been like receiving part of his wages in Bitcoin.

As a sn community we spend so much time talking about merchant adoption, payment infrastructure, and getting businesses to accept Bitcoin, that sometimes we forget about the people on the other side of those transactions, you can tell Adam thought it was cool too!

Adam said I could mention his name, so thanks again, Adam. Really appreciated the hospitality!

***

## The Good

I think what I enjoyed most about these two days wasn’t necessarily the payments themselves.

It was being around good wholesome people, I’m a sucker for that, and one of the many reasons I love going to church.

The night before, last night I was sitting in a room full of bitcoiners talking about self-custody, building projects that turn into companies, and the future of Bitcoin, I mean how cool is that!

The next afternoon, I was eating a burger with some of those same people, paying and slinging Lightning, and having a conversation with someone who earns part of his paycheck in sats, I mean how cool is that!

Two meals. Two Lightning payments. Not once did I have to explain what Bitcoin was. There’s something pretty remarkable about that, wasn’t always this way. Especially in places outside of Austin.

I’ve spent years talking about what Bitcoin adoption might look like. Sometimes it was easy for me to get lost in the arguments, bearish takes, fighting 💩coiners, and how everything is doom and gloom on the internet.

Then you go out into the real world, spend time with other bitcoiners, and realize that some of the things we’ve been talking about for years are quietly becoming normal and real world infrastructure all around you.

***

## Final Thoughts

You can spend all day on Stacker News, Nostr, or X talking about Bitcoin, but there’s still something special about sitting across the table from someone, sharing a meal, and getting to know the people who are actually using the things we all collectively build, it makes their life very enjoyable and we should all pick our heads up and see how much progress we’ve made collectively.

Anyway, if you’re in Dallas or Frisco, go get yourself a burger at Steak ’n Shake and pay with some sats.

And if you ever have the opportunity to attend the Dallas Bitcoin Meetup, I highly recommend it. Really good people doing some really good things in their community.

\*Question for you stackers I would love to hear about some of your favorite places to spend sats in the real world and how normal it’s become?\*

Someone [drinking homemade chai tea and eating banana bread](https://stacker.news/items/1613941/r/Bitter) while keeping a cat from stealing the loaf, which feels like the most honest Friday the 13th energy possible. Another person [tried a carnivore diet for a week](https://stacker.news/items/1610893/r/Bitter), living on beef, butter, salt, water, espresso and lime juice, no research, just a vague worry about the next few decades. The [cold-weather vegan recipes thread](https://stacker.news/items/1612125/r/Bitter) is looking for soups, stews and cookie ideas to welcome a vegan brother for Christmas, which is a nice puzzle to solve. On the pizza side, [pizza alla marinara](https://stacker.news/items/1610814/r/Bitter) got its history laid out as the oldest tomato pizza, a sailor's cheap staple from 1735, which makes me want to find one that actually lives up to that pedigree. Finally, [beef prices are staying high](https://stacker.news/items/1613160/r/Bitter) because the U.S. cattle herd is shrinking and Tyson shut a Utah plant, which is a supply chain fracture that will hit grocery shelves for a while.

If you were doing a carnivore week, what was the moment you actually felt different, or was it all just meat and monotony?

items.title: Always buy 2 pairs of eyeglasses
items.text: If you have to use eyeglasses, like anything they wear out. Just had to retire my first pair and on to the second this morning. Normally they last about 2-3 years before a new prescription is needed, but the first pair can wear out from regular, daily use. Having a second pair ready to go and new gives you a bump in vision with brand new, clear lenses and you don't have to stress about spending money months before a new prescription is likely going to happen. Usually a 2-fer is discounted to sell the eyeglasses. I always get mine at Costco as a pair.

items.title: The Billionaire Bankrolling of New, Physical Print Magazines
items.text:
Over five years ago, I wrote a piece called "[An Age of Patronage](https://thedailyeconomy.org/article/an-age-of-patronage/)" where I speculated how arts and research will/may work in a free world.

Basically sketching out the "value-for-value" revolution before that was cute or Lightning worked well enough for it.

## This month, I saw THREE print magazines launching/returning

**FIRST:** @asanoha and Bitcoin Art Magazine /Edition One https://stacker.news/items/1604664
This one isn't *quite* like the others -- for instance, I doubt there's a billionaire bankrolling it? -- but it's still a bet on a return to slow-form PHYSICAL MAGAZINES.

Definitely in the age of quick-hit/fast and hot takes AI slop, there's some.
Scarcity works like that, too: facing infinite generation, only the physical and human become scarce (https://stacker.news/items/1603955, https://stacker.news/items/1608788, https://stacker.news/items/1604664)

**SECOND:** LIFE magazine, a mainstay of 20th-century America, [is back](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/28/business/media/life-magazine-karlie-kloss.html). From that NYT article:

> The iconic magazine, known for its red-box logo and devotion to visual storytelling, will start publishing again next month as a quarterly print magazine.

*This*:

> It enters a fractured media landscape that is worlds away from the publication’s midcentury heights of acclaim, before the internet, social media and artificial intelligence upended the business model of magazine publishing.
> Daniel Okrent, who was the editor of Life magazine from 1992 to 1996, said that despite the value of the Life logo and the quality of the content, it was “a constantly unprofitable magazine” throughout history.

Also: run as a passion project/vanity thing for [small-time millionaire](https://www.celebritynetworth.com/richest-celebrities/models/karlie-kloss-net-worth/) and supermodel Karlie Kloss. Ruins Den's billionaire trend? No: husband is a [multibillionaire](https://www.eonline.com/news/1434962/inside-billionaire-josh-kushner-karlie-kloss-private-world). Funzies.

Also, importantly: NOT littered with ads. (Makes sense, since ad revenue isn't bankrolling them ANYWAY)

> The issue will come out on Nov. 23 as a large-format, 250-page print magazine retailing for $45, combining news photography with long-form journalism. There are no traditional print ads; instead the first issue is sponsored by Rivian and Figma.

says Wikipedia for why it closed its doors 25 years ago:

![](https://m.stacker.news/165194)

***

**THIRD:** Works in Progress.

Been seeing this a lot in my feed in recent weeks. (I imagine the algos heavily favor something you've visited/searched for recently) https://stacker.news/items/1591235, https://stacker.news/items/1598977, https://stacker.news/items/1601320

https://x.com/WorksInProgMag/status/2115617294005284869

No slop, *craft* in making beautiful things -- *and* important content.

The entire project is bankrolled by Stripe // Stripe Publishing and ultimate *their*owners, Patrick and John Collison et al.

***

It's *very* interesting to see this semi-/fake-capitalistic development, with art and storytelling and journalism be portrayed and worked on passionately by REAL and SERIOUS people, that looks and behaves like any other capitalist enterprise -- just *won't* be profit-oriented or ever aspire to making a profit.

## They're in it for the tech...

or rather, the humanity of it. The changing society. The craft and beauty and *deep meaning*.

I live this trend. And apparently, *sic semper salvatores*:

https://x.com/CharlesCMann/status/2118334333782012086

## All successful journalistic efforts were similarly "bankrolled by wealthy eccentrics"?

Yeah, I dunno. *But what did the rich ever do for us?!*

The recent anti-billionaire campaigns channeled their energy incorrectly. It's not that [the "rich" need to finance](https://thedailyeconomy.org/article/an-age-of-patronage/) failing programs like Medicare, or fat, lazy Californians' health problems. They should just build shit, bankroll artists, be \_patrons\_ to us creative peeps... and churches and architecture and all the other beautiful things in human/western civ. 

## "patronage is “the tribute which opulence owes to genius.” --Edmund Burke

> If you were wealthy, **it was your moral obligation to give back to the community** – not merely by improving the lot of the poor or renovating your local church but also by supporting artists and intellectuals.

Interesting future ahead of us. Huuuuge if true.

items.title: Chess improvement -- kill the mid-wit and find the elusive "spirit of chess"
items.text:
I was recently watching this [Chess Vibes video](https://www.youtube.com/live/zp0oiZGWRYw), where he tries to coach a ~1200 elo (presumably) adult improver, commenting on his games as he plays, and to use a Christian term, felt mildly *convicted* as I watched, as SpaceVega's sins reflected my own back to me. 

SpaceVega played beautiful openings. Actually watching some of his early Caro-Kann games, and how effortlessly he made it look to getting a really nice position, got me thinking I want to play that opening, and had me watching through [Eric Hansen's excellent run](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLUjxDD7HNNTjVEZ_1I8E28uav9t_ltDKX&si=wi3M2Ayt9WtTTJKy). 

(I have played the French, for my sins, and the Caro-Kann just looked like a more OP version, as SpaceVega would get the "bad" LSB out early and use it to wreck his opponent's pawn structure. But, really, Dash, you need to learn yet *another* opening? Is that going to help you stop hanging mate in one? Or playing unsound sacrifices?)

As I watched SpaceVega play more and more, get a great position out of the opening, then missing tactic after tactic, and eventually losing, or winning despite his best efforts to throw the game, making life hard for himself with poor conversion technique, it brought to mind an observation that I made about myself, and other adult improvers, that we often just focus on the *wrong* things (*cough* openings) when trying to improve at chess. 

I think one reason for this is that as adults drawn to chess, we are often attracted to the aesthetics of the game. We like the look of a nice position. We like to win with an opening trap in 9 moves and feel smart. We like to spend 100 or 1000s of dollars on opening courses, convincing ourselves that *just one more course* will finally propel us to our "true" rating. 

And what don't we like? Complications. Calculation. *Fighting*. Uncertainty. We don't like when a "pawn pusher" breaks all the opening principles and steamrolls our expensive London system "unfairly". We don't like time pressure. We just want to be left alone to recall our favorite lines and play in peace. 

And what about kids? You know, who are playing the game to have *fun* instead of attaching their fragile self-worth to a matching-algorithm number. Kids love *tactics*. They love forks. The love knights. They never miss a skewer. The strike at any tactical opportunity like a coiled snake. No sooner have you pushed your sweatily considered queen move when your vertically challenged antagonist has forked you with some bishop move. Instantly. Not even the courtesy to think about it first. 

Because chess is about *thinking* right? You go through your mental check list. You consider the *principles* of the game. What did Silman say about open files? That knight looks dangerous, but Ben Finegold told me never to push my f pawn.... You spend 5 mins on a move, recalling every book, every YouTube video, every Chessable course, meanwhile the kid just sees the tactic and takes your lady. 

Philidor said that "paws are the souls of chess". I think that "tactics are the spirit of chess". And I know, every beginner gets told to work on their tactics. This is not anything new or particularly interesting. But I think it's worth thinking about *why* tactics are so important when improving at chess. 

Because just like I think Silman's books are about thinking and fighting, and not really about "imbalances", I think tactics are about the "spirit of chess", which is to say, honing the instinct to pounce on your opponent's mistakes with a ruthless intensity. You need to somehow foster this mindset, or perhaps "mushin/ non-mind" as the Japanese martial artists may have described it. And that's going to take a lot of practice and pattern recognition. But more than anything, it's about backing yourself, trusting you calculation, and trying to get over the adult mid-wit fear of "what if I miss something?" which causes you to overthink, hesitate, or seek protection through the safety of the known, in excessive study of opening theory. 

It's like, you need to play chess to actually *play* chess, in order to get better at chess, if that makes sense. 
Maybe nonsense. Maybe there is just a hard limit related to biological determinism and the idea of chess improvement beyond a certain point is just alchemy. But some arbitrary pursuit of arcane knowledge/ secret wisdom is needed to keep the civilized mind occupied. May as well be chess. At least, it keeps me away from conspiracy theories and politics.
